correctness.rationale: For all real a>=1, the map first lands in x>=y. The negative cone is invariant and its affine matrix has eigenvalues strictly beyond ±1, with its virtual fixed point outside the cone. The positive cone also has two eigenvalues of modulus >1, leaving only its fixed point as a bounded forever-positive-cone orbit. Fourth-quadrant itineraries collapse to a positive diagonal scalar return t -> (1+2a-a²)t-(a+2): it has a feasible unique fixed t only when 1<=a<2, while every other trajectory escapes or falls into the invariant negative cone. The excluded upper-left quadrant enters the negative cone in at most two steps. Branchwise invertible positive/negative-cone preimages and rank-one fourth-quadrant preimages show all bounded orbits lie on countably many lines and points. Exact local branch multipliers and mathematical boundaries a=1,2 were checked. Standalone code corroborates identities, but the argument is universal and noncomputational.
